visual_base.visual_narrative_log: (1) A woman with short brown hair, wearing rounded black-rimmed glasses and a cream-colored knit sweater, sits in a modern office environment. She holds a small black lavalier microphone in her right hand, speaking with an expressive face and squinted eyes for emphasis. The background features a desk lamp, office supplies, and several branded gift bags in pink and red. White and yellow subtitles appear at the bottom center of the frame. (2) The scene cuts to a high-definition macro close-up of skin on a person's lower face, showing significant fine peeling and dry flaking near the chin and lips. The lighting is bright and clinical to accentuate the skin texture. (3) The camera returns to the woman, who continues speaking while gesturing with her hands to describe skin layers. An educational 3D graphic overlay then appears, showing a cross-section of skin cells; a red dashed circle and purple arrow highlight the upper epidermal layers as they begin to separate. (4) A brief humorous interlude features a white cat meme with a surprised expression in a small inset. The woman continues her explanation with hand-on-hand gestures. Another graphic follows, depicting grey, wavy layers representing skin flakes lifting off a surface. (5) A final macro close-up of peeling skin is shown, accompanied by a small cartoon cat icon and a 'NO' label. The woman concludes by pointing to her own face, while light-refraction graphics with sun and arrow icons illustrate how light bounces off uneven skin. The video ends with a clean white outro screen displaying the brand logo in black text.

narrative_and_purpose.narrativeStructure: List-based: Hook -> Explanation -> Scientific Proof -> Reassurance -> Branding
narrative_and_purpose.mainPurpose: This video serves as an educational skincare guide aimed at explaining a common side effect of Vitamin A (Retinol) use. By addressing the concern that 'skin looks darker or duller,' the narrator uses a mix of real-life skin close-ups and anatomical graphics to prove that the 'darkness' is actually caused by light reflection on peeling skin cells rather than permanent pigmentation. The ultimate goal is to reassure users to continue the product and subtly endorse the DRX Series Skincare brand.
